description.narrative: The project will improve the employability of graduates from technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programs and courses in three priority sectors of the economy in Mongolia: agriculture, construction, and road and transportation. The project, which has several innovative features, will (i) develop an industry-driven TVET system; (ii) upgrade selected TVET providers to implement competency-based training and assessment; (iii) establish training systems for TVET teachers and managers; (iv) support secondary education career guidance and schools that specialize in technology; and (v) establish an effective project management system.

Progress Toward Outcome: The project has been closed as of 31 August 2021. The MLSP has been working on the project closing activities which include acceptance of all the deliverables by the consultants and contractors, and preparation of the final audit and project completion report.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jul 2022: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45010/45010-002-apfs-en_3.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: The project performance management system was established in 2015, and the baseline data were collected in 2016. The quarterly and annual project progress reports are submitted generally on time. Learning and career guidance for eight and ninth grade students has been implemented in all schools since 2016. Career guidance has been extended to 10th-12th grade students at all schools with 10th-12th grades since 2018. The career guidance activity has been included in the instructional plan approved by education ministers orders No. A/103 in 2016 and No. A/491 in 2019. Learning and career guidance activities are being implemented as part of the extra-curricular activities during school regulated hours. Achieved ahead of time and exceeded the target. The project engaged 4 person/months of international and 14 person/months of national consultancy services on junior and senior secondary education career guidance. Two sets of career guidance materials (junior and senior secondary grade) developed and prepared that consists of workbooks for students, guidelines for teachers, parents, and school principals; and printed and distributed in 2016 and 2018. The project prepared 25 national trainers in career guidance. The trainers conducted training sessions nationwide in 2016, 2018 and 2019 and trained 14,031 people (82% female) including class teachers and school principals, training managers and social workers. More than 90% of eighth and ninth grade class teachers as part of school learning and career guidance teams were trained from 2016 to 2019. The 10th-12th grade class teachers (of whom more than 80% were women) were also trained in 2018 and 2019.Achieved. In total 6 person/months of international and 28 person/months of national consultancy services were engaged by the project to support the implementation of senior secondary STEM education curriculum in 2016-2020. The science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) education training modules were developed in 2016 for 10th grade and in 2018 for 12th grade; and delivered as materials for trainings organized under the project; and are being used as training tools in all schools nationwide. Senior secondary design and technology, math, chemistry, and physics teachers were trained in the new curriculum in 2016, 2018 and 2019. In total, in duplicated numbers 14,089 STEM subject teachers from all senior secondary schools attended nationwide training sessions in three years. Moreover, more than 600 TVET teachers participated in STEM subject training. In the framework of improving the learning environment for SSE STEM subjects, in total 555 schools were supplied with mathematics tools; 134 schools with physics; 100 schools with chemistry; 82 schools with design-technology laboratory equipment; and 316 schools with audio-video sets. All 555 schools were officially registered in the Education Sector Information System (ESIS) as recipients of these equipment and tools. The regional trainings on the use of STEM education lab equipment, supplied by the project, was conducted in 6 aimags and 3 districts of Ulaanbaatar city in October and November 2020. In total 641 (70% female) physics, chemistry, and design & technology teachers, and the Education and Culture Department specialists in charge of science and technology education participated in the trainings. To increase the results of TV lessons that were launched due to the COVID-19 school lockdown, the teaching methodologies in 7 subjects (senor secondary math, science, and design & technology) were developed, and 4 subjects (math, chemistry, physics, and design & technology) teaching methodologies were printed out and distributed to teachers in 2020.Achieved. Assessment and certification at VET AIMC and three assessment and certification centers (ACC) for the priority sectors have been established in 2021. The ACCs were established next to the Nalaikh TVET provider (road), Bayan-Chandmani TVET provider (agriculture), and Ulaanbaatar Polytechnic College (construction). All ACCs were rehabilitated and equipped with the training equipment. Test items and assessment tools for the key occupations were validated and approved by VET AIMC in December 2019. Standards for 15 key occupations in 3 priority sectors (construction, agriculture and road) have been approved by the National Council on VET and sector sub-councils. The TVET standards and CBT curriculum for 15 occupations in 3 priority sectors were approved by the order No. A/303 of the Minister of Labor and Social Protection in September 2019 and delivered to TVET providers for implementation. A two-stage training for TVET managers took place in February and June 2019 for 53 principals including 24 (44%) women from 36 TVET providers: (i) training conducted in February 2019; and (ii) training for the training managers conducted on 17-18 June 2019, delivered by the University of Finance and Economics. MLSP and TVET AIMC decided to organize a follow-up training for the TVET training managers and methodologists, a subject to COVID-19 situation. Specifically, the training on industry-driven TVET management and CBT methodology will be provided for 86 persons (78 training managers and methodologists of 39 public TVET schools and 4 regional methodology centers (RMC). All selected 19 TVET providers have been upgraded under the project by August 2021. The CBT pedagogy and assessment training for the TVET teachers was organized for 181 TVET teachers and staff members (63 female) on 6-10 May and 13-17 May 2019, respectively. The TVS training programs and cost estimates for the cascade training for TVET teachers of 13 occupations were developed and submitted to MLSP for approval. The short-term trainings are planned to be delivered in summer 2021 for 146 teachers for the key occupations through the assessment and certification centers and industries. Forty-nine (out of whom 25 female) teachers of the selected TVET providers, including 3 ACCs, were trained through industry placement as Master Trainers for 15 key occupations on 6-31 May 2019. Training was delivered by the training teams of professional associations, industry and university professors. However, only 30 of the master trainers remain at their positions as of May 2021. An international consulting firm TTT developed a training module and manual for training managers and methodologists on industry-driven TVET management, and delivered to the MLSP on 15 August 2019. The selection of the institution to develop and deliver this training program was done through open competitive selection. There were 5 applicants who expressed their interests, and the University of Finance and Economics (jointly with and Dale Carnegie Center) was selected to deliver the training. A 2-stage training for TVET managers took place in February and June 2019 for 53 principals including 24 (44%) women from 36 TVET providers: (i) training conducted in February 2019; and (ii) training for the training managers conducted on 17-18 June 2019, delivered by the University of Finance and Economics. In total 38 master trainers (of whom 28 women) for the CBT pedagogy and assessment completed 120-hour training program in March 2019, which was delivered in cooperation with industry associations and employers. The short-term technical and vocational skills training (TVS) programs for TVET teachers of 13 occupations were conducted in summer 2021.
